paper_metadata.title: Strengthening CoCrNi medium-entropy alloy by tuning lattice defects

evidence.quote: The CrCoNi medium-entropy alloy is not fully utilized at room temperature circumstance due to its low strength, despite excellent cryogenic mechanical properties.
The CoCrNi alloy bulk samples were synthesized using different normal material processing methods, i.e. spark plasma sintering (SPS), room temperature rolling and post-mortem annealing.
After rolling at 25 °C, the yield strength increased to 1.24 GPa, UTS increased to 1.41 GPa and the fracture strain presented at 7.0%.
the yield strength, UTS, and fracture strain of the CoCrNi alloys annealed at 600 °C for 1 h are 1.43 GPa, 1.61 GPa, and 2.3%, respectively.
At an annealing temperature of 700 °C, the yield strength (or the UTS) increased to 0.68 GPa (or 1.02 GPa), while the fracture strain became 27.6%.
SPS treatment was carried out at 1080 °C for 15 min under a uniaxial pressure of 40 MPa. Heating rate was set to be 100 °C/min. After SPS treatment, the CoCrNi samples were air cooled to 25 °C.
Then, rolling at 25 °C was applied to the CoCrNi samples to reduce its thickness by 50%.

The annealing of CoCrNi alloy samples was individually conducted in an electric resistance furnace at 600 °C and 700 °C. These annealed samples were subsequently cooled inside the furnace to reach 25 °C.

The annealing of CoCrNi alloy samples was individually conducted in an electric resistance furnace at 600 °C and 700 °C. These annealed samples were subsequently cooled inside the furnace to reach 25 °C.
XRD spectra identified only single f.c.c phase in all samples, as shown in Fig. S1(b).
The heterostructures (i.e. large grains mixed with small grains) were observed in all samples.
